items.stem: In an experiment Varun reacts 7.8 g of reactant A completely with 13.7 g of reactant B in a closed flask to form 15.1 g of product C and product D only. What mass of D is formed, and which law does the calculation use?
items.answer: 6.4 g; law of conservation of mass
items.markingKey: (c) 6.4 g; law of conservation of mass. Mass of reactants = mass of products: 7.8 + 13.7 = 15.1 + m(D), so m(D) = 6.4 g (1 mark); law of conservation of mass (1 mark).
options: 6.4 g; law of conservation of mass

items.stem: Which term describes the similarity in properties between certain second-period elements and the third-period elements diagonally below them?
items.answer: the diagonal relationship
items.markingKey: (d) The diagonal relationship: the similarity in properties between certain second-period elements and the third-period elements diagonally below them.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about quantum numbers and atomic orbitals is correct?
items.answer: Orbitals with l = 0 are spherically symmetrical.
items.markingKey: (b) Orbitals with l = 0 are spherically symmetrical. The other statements are false. A p orbital is dumb-bell shaped; s orbitals are spherical. In a multi-electron atom (e.g. K, Ca) 4s fills before 3d because it has a lower (n + l) value. It is impossible to know both exactly at the same time.
options: In a multi-electron atom 4s is higher in energy than 3d.
Orbitals with l = 0 are spherically symmetrical.
A p orbital is spherical in shape.
Heisenberg's principle says we can know the exact position and momentum of an electron.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct increasing order of reactivity towards electrophilic substitution?
items.answer: nitrobenzene < chlorobenzene < benzene < toluene
items.markingKey: (c) nitrobenzene < chlorobenzene < benzene < toluene. –NO₂ strongly deactivates, –Cl weakly deactivates, –CH₃ activates (+I, hyperconjugation), –OH strongly activates (+R).

items.stem: In Dumas' method, 0.35 g of an organic compound gave 25 mL of nitrogen measured at STP. Calculate the percentage of nitrogen. (1 mol of N₂ occupies 22400 mL at STP)
Which of the following shows the correct increasing order of dipole moment?
items.answer: CCl₄ < NF₃ < NH₃ < H₂O
items.markingKey: (d) CCl₄ < NF₃ < NH₃ < H₂O. CCl₄ is zero (symmetric); in NF₃ the lone-pair moment opposes the bond moments; NH₃ (1.47 D) is lower than H₂O (1.85 D).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about spontaneity, entropy and Gibbs energy is incorrect?
items.answer: All exothermic reactions are spontaneous.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “All exothermic reactions are spontaneous.” Correct form: An exothermic reaction with large negative ΔS can be non-spontaneous at high temperature.
options: A negative ΔH alone does not guarantee spontaneity.
The entropy of a gas is greater than that of the same substance as a liquid.

items.stem: Which term describes a solution that resists change in pH on dilution or on addition of small amounts of acid or alkali?
items.answer: a buffer solution
items.markingKey: (d) A buffer solution: a solution that resists change in pH on dilution or on addition of small amounts of acid or alkali.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT an oxidation according to the classical concept?
items.answer: CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O (for CuO)
items.markingKey: (c) CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O (for CuO) is a reduction according to the classical concept, not an oxidation according to the classical concept.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about matter and its properties is correct?
items.answer: In a homogeneous mixture the composition is uniform throughout.
items.markingKey: (c) In a homogeneous mixture the composition is uniform throughout. The other statements are false. The SI unit of mass is the kilogram. Burning of a candle involves a chemical change (combustion) as well as melting. The properties of a compound are different from those of its constituent elements.
options: Burning of a candle involves only physical change.
The properties of a compound are the same as those of its constituent elements.
In a homogeneous mixture the composition is uniform throughout.
The SI unit of mass is the gram.

items.stem: What is meant by “a group”?
items.answer: A vertical column of the periodic table.
items.markingKey: (a) A vertical column of the periodic table.. 1 mark: a vertical column of the periodic table.
options: A vertical column of the periodic table.
A horizontal row of the periodic table
The observation that in groups of three similar elements the atomic weight of the middle element is about the mean of the other two
The law that the physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers

items.stem: Which term describes the quantum number that determines the shape of an orbital (subshell)?
items.answer: the azimuthal quantum number
items.markingKey: (b) The azimuthal quantum number: the quantum number that determines the shape of an orbital (subshell).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The energy difference between eclipsed and staggered ethane is about 12.5 kJ mol⁻¹.
Reason (R): Alkanes readily undergo addition reactions.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Alkanes are saturated; they undergo substitution, not addition.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Sodium fusion extract is boiled with HNO₃ before testing for halogens.
Reason (R): Cyanide and sulphide ions, if present, would give a precipitate with AgNO₃.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Boiling with HNO₃ removes CN⁻ and S²⁻ that would interfere.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): H₂O has a net dipole moment.
Reason (R): H₂O is a bent molecule, so its bond dipoles do not cancel.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Bent shape leaves a resultant dipole of 1.85 D.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): For the reaction H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) → 2HCl(g), ΔH = ΔU.
Reason (R): Δn_g for this reaction is zero.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) ΔH = ΔU + Δn_gRT with Δn_g = 2 − 2 = 0.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Calculate the pH of a 5.0 × 10⁻³ M aqueous solution of KOH at 298 K.
A galvanic cell is made from the Mg²⁺/Mg and Ag⁺/Ag electrodes. E°(Mg²⁺/Mg) = −2.36 V and E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = +0.80 V. Which electrode is the anode, and what is the standard emf of the cell?
items.answer: Anode: Mg²⁺/Mg; E°cell = 3.16 V
items.markingKey: The couple with the lower reduction potential (Mg²⁺/Mg) is oxidised at the anode (1); E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.80 − (−2.36) = 3.16 V (1).

items.stem: Two oxides of iron contain 160 g and 240 g of oxygen respectively combined with 560 g of iron. Show that these data illustrate the law of multiple proportions.
items.answer: Masses of oxygen combining with a fixed mass of iron are in the ratio 2 : 3, a simple whole-number ratio.
items.markingKey: Fixed mass of iron = 560 g; 160 : 240 = 2 : 3 (simple whole numbers), as in FeO and Fe₂O₃ – 2 marks.

items.stem: Give two differences between p-block and s-block.
items.answer: P-block: contain the halogens and noble gases; include metals, non-metals and metalloids. S-block: alkali and alkaline earth metals; mostly reactive metals with low ionisation enthalpies.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. p-block – contain the halogens and noble gases; include metals, non-metals and metalloids; s-block – alkali and alkaline earth metals; mostly reactive metals with low ionisation enthalpies.

items.stem: Give two differences between Bohr's model and Rutherford's nuclear model.
items.answer: Bohr's model: energy is emitted only when an electron jumps from a higher to a lower orbit; the angular momentum of the electron is quantised. Rutherford's nuclear model: most of the space in the atom is empty; the positive charge and most of the mass are concentrated in a tiny nucleus.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. Bohr's model – energy is emitted only when an electron jumps from a higher to a lower orbit; the angular momentum of the electron is quantised; Rutherford's nuclear model – most of the space in the atom is empty; the positive charge and most of the mass are concentrated in a tiny nucleus.

items.stem: How do polynuclear hydrocarbons cause cancer?
items.answer: After entering the body they undergo biochemical reactions (metabolic activation) and finally damage DNA, causing uncontrolled cell division (cancer).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: biochemical changes; 1 mark: DNA damage.

items.stem: In Kjeldahl's method, the ammonia evolved from 1.00 g of an organic compound was exactly neutralised by 25 mL of 0.05 M H₂SO₄. Calculate the percentage of nitrogen.
Write two resonance-free Lewis structures for CO₂: O=C=O and O≡C–O. Use formal charges to decide which is preferred.
items.answer: O=C=O: all formal charges 0. O≡C–O: +1 on the triply bonded O, −1 on the singly bonded O. The structure with zero formal charges (O=C=O) is preferred.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: formal charges on both; 1 mark: lowest formal charges preferred.

items.stem: The equilibrium constant of a reaction at 298 K is 0.010. Calculate ΔG° for the reaction. (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
items.answer: 11.41 kJ mol⁻¹

items.stem: In the manufacture of ammonia (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, ΔH = −92.4 kJ mol⁻¹) a low temperature favours a high yield, yet about 700 K is used. Explain this choice.
items.answer: At low temperature the equilibrium yield is high but the rate is too slow; about 700 K with an iron catalyst and ~200 atm gives an acceptable yield at a fast rate (optimum conditions).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: low T favours yield but slow; 1 mark: compromise temperature with catalyst for rate.

items.stem: Calculate the oxidation number of C in CH₄ and of N in N₂H₄.
items.answer: C in CH₄: −4; N in N₂H₄: −2
items.markingKey: Sum of oxidation numbers equals the charge on the species; 1 mark each: −4 and −2.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct increasing order of length: 1 μm, 1 mm, 1 dm, 1 pm. Give a reason.
items.answer: 1 pm < 1 μm < 1 mm < 1 dm
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order 1 pm < 1 μm < 1 mm < 1 dm; 1 mark for the reason: pico = 10⁻¹², nano = 10⁻⁹, micro = 10⁻⁶, milli = 10⁻³, centi = 10⁻², deci = 10⁻¹.

items.stem:
An element has these characteristics: placed separately at the bottom of the table; lanthanoids and actinoids; outer configuration (n−2)f¹⁻¹⁴ (n−1)d⁰⁻¹ ns².
(i) To which block of the periodic table does it belong? (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were s-block? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) F-block (ii) actinoids are radioactive (iii) form mostly ionic compounds (except Li and Be); outer configuration ns¹ or ns²
items.markingKey: (i) f-block – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: actinoids are radioactive – 1 mark. (iii) for s-block: alkali and alkaline earth metals; outer configuration ns¹ or ns²; mostly reactive metals with low ionisation enthalpies – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem:
An observation from an experiment is: the positive charge is spread uniformly through the atom; electrons are embedded like seeds in a watermelon.
(i) Which atomic model or conclusion does it support? (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were Bohr's model? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Thomson's plum pudding model (ii) mass is assumed to be distributed uniformly (iii) electrons revolve in fixed circular orbits of definite energy; the angular momentum of the electron is quantised
items.markingKey: (i) Thomson's plum pudding model – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: mass is assumed to be distributed uniformly – 1 mark. (iii) for Bohr's model: electrons revolve in fixed circular orbits of definite energy; energy is emitted only when an electron jumps from a higher to a lower orbit; the angular momentum of the electron is quantised – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Draw (describe) the Newman projections of the staggered and eclipsed conformations of ethane. (a) Which is more stable and why? (b) What is the energy difference? (c) Why cannot the two be isolated? (d) What is meant by the dihedral angle in the two forms?
items.answer: Staggered: rear H atoms at 60° to front ones; eclipsed: rear H atoms directly behind front ones. (a) Staggered, minimum torsional strain. (b) ~12.5 kJ mol⁻¹. (c) The barrier is small, so rotation is rapid at room temperature. (d) Angle between C–H bonds on adjacent carbons: 60° staggered, 0° eclipsed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark diagrams; 1 mark each (a)-(d).

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between heterolytic fission and homolytic fission on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A bond in a reaction breaks in this way: favoured by polar solvents. Identify the type of bond fission – heterolytic fission or homolytic fission? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Heterolytic fission: one atom keeps both electrons of the bonding pair; a carbocation and an anion (or carbanion and cation) are formed; favoured by polar solvents. Homolytic fission: each atom keeps one electron of the bonding pair; free radicals are formed; favoured by heat, light or peroxides and non-polar solvents. (b) Heterolytic fission.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: heterolytic fission; 1 mark: “favoured by polar solvents” is a feature of heterolytic fission.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between sp³ and sp³d on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A central atom has the following hybridisation features: tetrahedral arrangement. Identify the type of hybridisation – sp³ or sp³d? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Sp³: four hybrid orbitals at 109.5°; 25% s character; found in CH₄ and C₂H₆. Sp³d: five hybrid orbitals; three equatorial and two axial positions; found in PCl₅. (b) Sp³.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: sp³; 1 mark: “tetrahedral arrangement” is a feature of sp³.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the classification of elements is incorrect?
items.answer: Eka-silicon was later discovered as gallium.
items.markingKey: (d) The incorrect statement is “Eka-silicon was later discovered as gallium.” Correct form: Eka-silicon is germanium; eka-aluminium is gallium.
options: Moseley showed that atomic number is a more fundamental property than atomic mass.
The modern periodic table has 18 groups and 7 periods.
The position of isotopes was a problem in Mendeleev's periodic table.
Eka-silicon was later discovered as gallium.

items.stem: Which term describes a system that exchanges neither energy nor matter with the surroundings?
items.answer: an isolated system
items.markingKey: (a) An isolated system: a system that exchanges neither energy nor matter with the surroundings.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the mole concept is correct?
items.answer: The molecular formula is a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula.
items.markingKey: (b) The molecular formula is a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula. The other statements are false. The empirical formula of benzene is CH; C₆H₆ is its molecular formula. They contain different numbers of molecules because their molar masses (2 and 32 g mol⁻¹) differ. They can be the same, e.g. H₂O, CO₂ and CH₄.
options: The empirical formula of benzene is C₆H₆.
The molecular formula is a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula.
1 g of hydrogen gas and 1 g of oxygen gas contain the same number of molecules.
The empirical and molecular formulae of a compound can never be the same.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about oxidation number and types of redox reactions is incorrect?
items.answer: The oxidation number of hydrogen is +1 in all its compounds.
items.markingKey: (c) The incorrect statement is “The oxidation number of hydrogen is +1 in all its compounds.” Correct form: In metal hydrides (NaH, CaH₂) hydrogen is −1.
options: The sum of oxidation numbers in a polyatomic ion equals its charge.
In peroxides oxygen has an oxidation number of −1.
The oxidation number of hydrogen is +1 in all its compounds.
Hydrogen has an oxidation number of −1 in metal hydrides such as NaH.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about alkynes is incorrect?
items.answer: Ethyne is less acidic than ethene.
items.markingKey: (b) The incorrect statement is “Ethyne is less acidic than ethene.” Correct form: Ethyne is more acidic because sp carbon has 50% s character.
options: But-2-yne does not react with sodamide to give a salt.
Ethyne is less acidic than ethene.
Ethyne can be prepared from calcium carbide and water.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct increasing order of lattice enthalpy?
items.answer: KCl < NaCl < LiCl
items.markingKey: (b) KCl < NaCl < LiCl. Smaller cation, closer ions and stronger attraction: K⁺ > Na⁺ > Li⁺ in size.

items.stem: The pair ¹⁴C and ¹⁴N are best described as …
items.answer: isobars
items.markingKey: (a) Isobars: same A (14), different Z.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about weak electrolytes, buffers and salt hydrolysis is incorrect?
items.answer: A solution of CH₃COONa is acidic.
items.markingKey: (c) The incorrect statement is “A solution of CH₃COONa is acidic.” Correct form: Acetate ions hydrolyse to give OH⁻, so the solution is basic.
options: Blood is buffered at a pH of about 7.4.
An aqueous solution of NH₄Cl is acidic.
A solution of CH₃COONa is acidic.
The degree of ionisation of a weak acid increases on dilution.

items.stem: A mixture or compound has these properties: used for camphor, naphthalene or benzoic acid; the compound changes directly from solid to vapour on heating. Which method of purification is most suitable?
items.answer: sublimation
items.markingKey: (b) Sublimation: used for camphor, naphthalene or benzoic acid; the compound changes directly from solid to vapour on heating.

items.stem: An element has these characteristics: actinoids are radioactive; placed separately at the bottom of the table. To which block of the periodic table does it belong?
items.answer: f-block
items.markingKey: (d) F-block: actinoids are radioactive; placed separately at the bottom of the table.

items.stem: For a reaction: ΔH is negative and ΔS is positive; both terms in ΔG = ΔH − TΔS are negative. Under what conditions is the reaction spontaneous?
items.answer: spontaneous at all temperatures
items.markingKey: (c) Spontaneous at all temperatures: ΔH is negative and ΔS is positive; both terms in ΔG = ΔH − TΔS are negative.

items.stem: Priya dissolves 0.3 g of urea (NH₂CONH₂) in water and makes the solution up to 100 mL in a volumetric flask. Calculate the molarity. (Molar mass = 60 g mol⁻¹)

Assertion (A): A more negative E° means a stronger reducing agent.
Reason (R): Fluorine is the strongest reducing agent in the electrochemical series.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: F₂ has the highest E° and is the strongest oxidising agent.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): But-2-yne does not form a sodium salt.
Reason (R): But-2-yne has no hydrogen on a triply bonded carbon.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Only ≡C–H hydrogens are acidic.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): BF₃ does not obey the octet rule.
Reason (R): Boron has only three valence electrons to share.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Sharing three electrons gives B only six electrons in BF₃.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Increasing the intensity of light increases the kinetic energy of photoelectrons.
Reason (R): Electrons are ejected without any time lag when light of suitable frequency strikes the metal.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Intensity increases the number of photoelectrons; their kinetic energy depends on frequency. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as Lewis acid or Lewis base: OH⁻, AlCl₃, C₂H₅OC₂H₅, Co³⁺.
items.answer: OH⁻ – Lewis base; AlCl₃ – Lewis acid; C₂H₅OC₂H₅ – Lewis base; Co³⁺ – Lewis acid.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: OH⁻ – Lewis base; AlCl₃ – Lewis acid; C₂H₅OC₂H₅ – Lewis base; Co³⁺ – Lewis acid.

items.stem: Give two differences between simple distillation and differential extraction.
items.answer: Simple distillation: two liquids differ widely in boiling points (e.g. chloroform 334 K and aniline 457 K); the liquids do not decompose at their boiling points. Differential extraction: a separating funnel is used; the two solvents are immiscible.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. simple distillation – two liquids differ widely in boiling points (e.g. chloroform 334 K and aniline 457 K); the liquids do not decompose at their boiling points; differential extraction – a separating funnel is used; the two solvents are immiscible.

items.stem: An element has the electronic configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁴. State its period, group and block in the modern periodic table.
items.answer: Period 2, group 16, p-block
items.markingKey: Highest n = 2 ⇒ period 2; last electron enters p subshell ⇒ p-block; group 16 from the number of valence (ns + np, or ns + (n−1)d) electrons.

items.stem: A gas expands isothermally against a constant external pressure of 3 bar from 1 L to 16 L. Calculate the work done in joules. (1 L bar = 100 J)
items.markingKey: w = −p_ext ΔV = −3 × (16 − 1) = −45 L bar = −4500 J (work done by the system, so negative).

items.stem: The empirical formula of a compound is HO and its molar mass is 34 g mol⁻¹. What is its molecular formula?
items.answer: H₂O₂
items.markingKey: Empirical formula mass = 17; n = 34/17 = 2; molecular formula = (HO)ₙ = H₂O₂.

items.stem: Balance the following redox reaction in acidic medium by the ion–electron (half-reaction) method: MnO₄⁻ + SO₂ → Mn²⁺ + SO₄²⁻
items.answer: 2MnO₄⁻ + 5SO₂ + 2H₂O → 2Mn²⁺ + 5SO₄²⁻ + 4H⁺
items.markingKey: Write oxidation and reduction half reactions; balance atoms other than O and H, then O with H₂O, H with H⁺, charge with electrons; multiply so electrons cancel (MnO₄⁻ gains 5 e⁻ each). Result: 2MnO₄⁻ + 5SO₂ + 2H₂O → 2Mn²⁺ + 5SO₄²⁻ + 4H⁺. (3 marks: 1 each half reaction, 1 final)

items.stem: How will you distinguish but-1-yne from but-2-yne by a chemical test? Explain.
items.answer: But-1-yne (terminal) gives a precipitate with ammoniacal AgNO₃ (Tollens') or ammoniacal Cu₂Cl₂ / liberates H₂ with Na; but-2-yne does not, as it lacks an acidic ≡C–H.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: test and observation; 1 mark: reason (acidic terminal H).

items.stem: Give two differences between sp² and sp³d².
items.answer: Sp²: trigonal planar arrangement; found in BF₃ and ethene. Sp³d²: found in SF₆; octahedral arrangement.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. sp² – trigonal planar arrangement; found in BF₃ and ethene; sp³d² – found in SF₆; octahedral arrangement.

items.stem: Why does the hydrogen atom, which has only one electron, show so many lines in its spectrum?
items.answer: A sample has a very large number of atoms; different atoms are excited to different levels and fall back by different transitions, each giving a line of a definite frequency.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: many atoms in different excited states; 1 mark: each transition between two levels gives one line.

items.stem: Sugar dissolves in water until the solution is saturated, after which extra sugar stays undissolved. How could you show that the saturated solution is in dynamic equilibrium?
items.answer: Add a little radioactively labelled sugar to the saturated solution: radioactivity soon appears both in the solution and in the solid, showing dissolution and crystallisation continue at equal rates.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: labelled (radioactive) sugar; 1 mark: exchange observed between solid and solution.

items.stem: Give two differences between homolytic fission and heterolytic fission.
items.answer: Homolytic fission: free radicals are formed; each atom keeps one electron of the bonding pair. Heterolytic fission: one atom keeps both electrons of the bonding pair; a carbocation and an anion (or carbanion and cation) are formed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. homolytic fission – free radicals are formed; each atom keeps one electron of the bonding pair; heterolytic fission – one atom keeps both electrons of the bonding pair; a carbocation and an anion (or carbanion and cation) are formed.

items.stem: Why is the modern periodic law based on atomic number and not on atomic mass? Give one anomaly of Mendeleev's table it removes.
items.answer: Properties depend on electronic configuration, which is set by atomic number. It removes anomalies like Ar (39.9) before K (39.1) and Co before Ni, and the position of isotopes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: properties depend on Z/electronic configuration; 1 mark: one anomaly resolved.

items.stem:
The true mass of a sample is 2.15 g. Three students weighed it three times each.
Manish: 2.14, 2.15, 2.15 g
Student B: 2.59, 2.59, 2.59 g
Student C: 1.85, 2.21, 2.45 g
(i) Whose readings are both precise and accurate? (1 mark)
(ii) Whose readings are precise but not accurate? (1 mark)
(iii) Distinguish between precision and accuracy. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Manish (ii) Student B (iii) Precision is closeness of repeated readings to each other; accuracy is closeness to the true value.
items.markingKey: (i) Manish: readings close to each other and to 2.15 g (1). (ii) B: close together but about 0.44 g high (1). (iii) precision – agreement among measurements; accuracy – agreement with the true value (1 + 1).

items.stem:
A survey found that workers in coal-tar processing units and chimney sweeps had higher rates of skin cancer than office workers.
(i) Name one carcinogen likely to be present in coal tar. (1 mark)
(ii) What structural feature do such carcinogens share? (1 mark)
(iii) Suggest two safety measures for these workers. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) 1,2-benzpyrene (or 3-methylcholanthrene / 1,2-benzanthracene). (ii) More than two fused benzene rings (polynuclear aromatic). (iii) Protective clothing and gloves; masks and ventilation; washing skin; regular health checks.
items.markingKey: (i) 1 (ii) 1 (iii) 1 each for two measures.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between sp³ and sp on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A central atom has the following hybridisation features: found in CH₄ and C₂H₆. Identify the type of hybridisation – sp³ or sp? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Sp³: four hybrid orbitals at 109.5°; 25% s character; found in CH₄ and C₂H₆. Sp: two hybrid orbitals at 180°; 50% s character; found in BeCl₂ and ethyne. (b) Sp³.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: sp³; 1 mark: “found in CH₄ and C₂H₆” is a feature of sp³.

items.stem: An electron in a hydrogen atom falls from n = 5 to n = 2. Calculate the wavelength of the radiation emitted and name the spectral series. (R_H = 109 677 cm⁻¹)
items.answer: 434.2 nm; Balmer series (visible)
items.markingKey: ν̄ = R_H(1/2² − 1/5²) = 23032 cm⁻¹ (1); λ = 1/ν̄ = 434.2 nm (1); final level n = 2 ⇒ Balmer series (1).

items.stem: Calculate the molar solubility of AgCl (Ksp = 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰) in a 0.01 M solution of NaCl, and compare it with its solubility in pure water.
items.answer: 1.80 × 10⁻⁸ mol L⁻¹ (in water 1.34 × 10⁻⁵ mol L⁻¹); solubility is lowered by the common ion
items.markingKey: Ksp = s(s + 0.01) ≈ s × 0.01 ⇒ s = 1.80 × 10⁻⁸ mol L⁻¹ (2); in pure water s = 1.34 × 10⁻⁵ mol L⁻¹, so the common ion suppresses solubility (1).

items.stem: Which of the following is a group showing −R (electron-withdrawing resonance) effect?
items.answer: –COCH₃
items.markingKey: (d) –COCH₃ is a group showing −R (electron-withdrawing resonance) effect; the others are not.

items.stem: Which of the following is a salt whose aqueous solution is neutral?
items.answer: NaCl
items.markingKey: (c) NaCl is a salt whose aqueous solution is neutral; the others are not.

items.stem: Which term describes the product of the magnitude of the charge and the distance between the centres of positive and negative charge?
items.answer: dipole moment
items.markingKey: (c) Dipole moment: the product of the magnitude of the charge and the distance between the centres of positive and negative charge.

items.stem: Which of the following is a path function?
items.answer: work
items.markingKey: (b) Work is a path function; the others are not.

items.stem: Which term describes the number of moles of solute per kilogram of solvent?
items.answer: molality
items.markingKey: (c) Molality: the number of moles of solute per kilogram of solvent.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about redox reactions and electrode processes is correct?
items.answer: In a galvanic cell oxidation takes place at the anode.
items.markingKey: (d) In a galvanic cell oxidation takes place at the anode. The other statements are false. In a galvanic cell the cathode is positive; the anode (where oxidation occurs) is negative. E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) > E°(Zn²⁺/Zn), so copper cannot reduce Zn²⁺. F₂ has the highest E° and is the strongest oxidising agent.
options: Fluorine is the strongest reducing agent in the electrochemical series.
In a galvanic cell the cathode is the negative electrode.
Copper can displace zinc from zinc sulphate solution.
In a galvanic cell oxidation takes place at the anode.

items.stem: Electrons in a sample of hydrogen atoms are excited to the n = 8 level. What is the maximum number of spectral lines that can be emitted as they return to the ground state?
items.markingKey: (c) 28. Number of lines = n(n − 1)/2 = 8 × 7/2 = 28.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a d-block element?
items.answer: neodymium
items.markingKey: (a) Neodymium is an f-block element, not a d-block element.

items.stem: What volume of oxygen is needed for complete combustion of 20 mL of heptane (C₇H₁₆), all volumes at the same temperature and pressure? Write the balanced equation.
items.answer: 220 mL
items.markingKey: (b) 220 mL. CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ + (3n + 1)/2 O₂ → nCO₂ + (n + 1)H₂O; for n = 7: 1 : 11 by volume (1) ⇒ 220 mL (1).

items.stem: Which of the following is an acyclic (open-chain) compound?
items.answer: isobutane
items.markingKey: (d) Isobutane is an acyclic (open-chain) compound; the others are not.

items.stem: What is the conjugate acid of NH₂⁻?
items.answer: NH₃
items.markingKey: (b) Adding H⁺ to NH₂⁻ gives its conjugate acid NH₃.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about bond parameters, resonance and polarity is incorrect?
items.answer: The unit of dipole moment is the newton.
items.markingKey: (b) The incorrect statement is “The unit of dipole moment is the newton.” Correct form: Dipole moment is measured in debye (1 D = 3.336 × 10⁻³⁰ C m).
options: Bond length decreases as bond order increases.
The unit of dipole moment is the newton.
The dipole moment of NH₃ is greater than that of NF₃.
CO₂ has zero dipole moment because it is linear.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A spontaneous reaction must be fast.
Reason (R): A reaction with ΔG < 0 is spontaneous at constant temperature and pressure.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Spontaneity says nothing about rate; e.g. diamond → graphite is spontaneous but extremely slow. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A temperature on the kelvin scale can never be negative.
Reason (R): Absolute zero, 0 K, is the lowest possible temperature.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Since nothing can be colder than 0 K, kelvin temperatures are zero or positive; R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Lithium is the strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution.
Reason (R): Li⁺/Li has the most negative standard reduction potential.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) E° = −3.05 V means the greatest tendency to lose electrons.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Photoelectrons are not emitted below the threshold frequency, whatever the intensity of light.
Reason (R): The energy of one photon (hν) must at least equal the work function to eject one electron.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Each electron is ejected by one photon, so the photon energy, not intensity, decides emission.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: An element has the IUPAC temporary name “unnilquadium”. What is its atomic number and symbol?
items.answer: Z = 104; Unq
items.markingKey: Each root stands for a digit: unnilquadium → 104; symbol Unq.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Polynuclear hydrocarbons are formed by complete combustion of fuels.”
items.answer: They are formed by incomplete combustion of organic matter.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: They are formed by incomplete combustion of organic matter.

items.stem: A mixture or compound has these properties: used to purify sugar or benzoic acid from water; it is sparingly soluble in the cold solvent but well soluble when hot. Which method of purification is most suitable? Give a reason.
items.answer: Crystallisation
items.markingKey: 1 mark: crystallisation; 1 mark: the features used to purify sugar or benzoic acid from water; it is sparingly soluble in the cold solvent but well soluble when hot are characteristic of it.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “A mixture of HCl and NaCl is a buffer.”
items.answer: HCl is a strong acid; a buffer needs a weak acid and its salt (or weak base and its salt).
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: HCl is a strong acid; a buffer needs a weak acid and its salt (or weak base and its salt).

items.stem: How many valence electrons must be shown in the Lewis structure of HCN?
Give two differences between spontaneous only at low temperature and non-spontaneous at all temperatures.
items.answer: Spontaneous only at low temperature: ΔH is negative and ΔS is negative; ΔH outweighs TΔS when T < ΔH/ΔS. Non-spontaneous at all temperatures: the reverse reaction is spontaneous at all temperatures; ΔG is always positive.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. spontaneous only at low temperature – ΔH is negative and ΔS is negative; ΔH outweighs TΔS when T < ΔH/ΔS; non-spontaneous at all temperatures – the reverse reaction is spontaneous at all temperatures; ΔG is always positive.

items.stem: Calculate the molecular (formula) mass of potassium chloride, KCl. (Atomic masses: K = 39, Cl = 35.5 u)
Calculate the oxidation number of Cl in ClO₄⁻ and of S in S₄O₆²⁻.
items.answer: Cl in ClO₄⁻: +7; S in S₄O₆²⁻: +5/2
items.markingKey: Sum of oxidation numbers equals the charge on the species; 1 mark each: +7 and +5/2.

items.stem: In a discharge tube the charge-to-mass ratio of cathode-ray particles is the same whatever gas fills the tube or whatever metal the cathode is made of. What does this show? How do canal rays differ in this respect?
items.answer: Electrons are a basic constituent of all atoms (e/mₑ = 1.758820 × 10¹¹ C kg⁻¹). The e/m of canal-ray particles depends on the gas, since they are positive ions of that gas.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: same e/m ⇒ electrons present in all atoms; 1 mark: canal-ray e/m depends on the gas (lightest from H₂ = proton).

items.stem: Element 114 (ununquadium, Uuq) has not been characterised fully. Predict its period, group and block, and name the family it would belong to.
items.answer: Period 7, group 14, p-block; group 14 elements
items.markingKey: Period 7 ends at Z = 118 (7p⁶). Z = 114 lies in 7p: 7s² 5f¹⁴ 6d¹⁰ 7p² ⇒ group 14 (1 + 1).

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Conformations of ethane can be separated at room temperature.”
items.answer: The rotational barrier is small (12.5 kJ mol⁻¹), so they interconvert rapidly and cannot be isolated.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The rotational barrier is small (12.5 kJ mol⁻¹), so they interconvert rapidly and cannot be isolated.

items.stem: How many structural isomers are possible for the molecular formula C₄H₉Br? Name them.
items.answer: 4: 1-bromobutane, 2-bromobutane, 1-bromo-2-methylpropane, 2-bromo-2-methylpropane
items.markingKey: 4 isomers (1 mark); naming them: 1-bromobutane, 2-bromobutane, 1-bromo-2-methylpropane, 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (1 mark).

items.stem:
A central atom has the following hybridisation features: six hybrid orbitals at 90°; found in SF₆; uses two d orbitals.
(i) Identify the type of hybridisation. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were sp? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Sp³d² (ii) octahedral arrangement (iii) two hybrid orbitals at 180°; 50% s character
items.markingKey: (i) sp³d² – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: octahedral arrangement – 1 mark. (iii) for sp: two hybrid orbitals at 180°; 50% s character; found in BeCl₂ and ethyne – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem:
The true mass of a sample is 4.37 g. Three students weighed it three times each.
Siddharth: 4.37, 4.37, 4.37 g
Student B: 4.93, 4.94, 4.95 g
Student C: 4.03, 4.44, 4.71 g
(i) Whose readings are both precise and accurate? (1 mark)
(ii) Whose readings are precise but not accurate? (1 mark)
(iii) Distinguish between precision and accuracy. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Siddharth (ii) Student B (iii) Precision is closeness of repeated readings to each other; accuracy is closeness to the true value.
items.markingKey: (i) Siddharth: readings close to each other and to 4.37 g (1). (ii) B: close together but about 0.57 g high (1). (iii) precision – agreement among measurements; accuracy – agreement with the true value (1 + 1).

items.stem: Balance the following redox reaction in acidic medium by the ion–electron (half-reaction) method: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + Fe²⁺ → Cr³⁺ + Fe³⁺
items.answer: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 6Fe²⁺ + 14H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 6Fe³⁺ + 7H₂O
items.markingKey: Write oxidation and reduction half reactions; balance atoms other than O and H, then O with H₂O, H with H⁺, charge with electrons; multiply so electrons cancel (Cr₂O₇²⁻ gains 6 e⁻ each). Result: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 6Fe²⁺ + 14H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 6Fe³⁺ + 7H₂O. (3 marks: 1 each half reaction, 1 final)

items.stem: An electron in a hydrogen atom falls from n = 4 to n = 1. Calculate the wavelength of the radiation emitted and name the spectral series. (R_H = 109 677 cm⁻¹)
items.answer: 97.3 nm; Lyman series (ultraviolet)
items.markingKey: ν̄ = R_H(1/1² − 1/4²) = 102822 cm⁻¹ (1); λ = 1/ν̄ = 97.3 nm (1); final level n = 1 ⇒ Lyman series (1).

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between d-block and s-block on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An element has these characteristics: used widely as catalysts. To which block of the periodic table does it belong – d-block or s-block? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) D-block: outer configuration (n−1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns⁰⁻²; mostly form coloured ions; show variable oxidation states. S-block: alkali and alkaline earth metals; outer configuration ns¹ or ns²; mostly reactive metals with low ionisation enthalpies. (b) D-block.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: d-block; 1 mark: “used widely as catalysts” is a feature of d-block.
